title: Tenant-aware gradual control plane reconciliation with canary telemetry gates
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background: Private (VPC) control plane upgrades have historically been all-or-nothing or wave-based by region. We need a safer, tenant-aware promotion approach that reconciles control plane versions gradually while prioritizing high-SLA tenants and using telemetry gates to reduce blast radius.

Scope: Implement orchestration and Terraform/IaC primitives plus runtime hooks to support: (1) tenant-scoped reconciliation groups, (2) staged promotion windows driven by telemetry (error rate, API latency P95, rollout health), (3) automated preflight and postflight checks, (4) rollback automation and short-circuiting, (5) auditable runbooks and release artifacts. This ticket includes design, Terraform module updates, control-plane operator changes (reconciliation logic), and dashboards/alerts.

Proposal:
- Introduce a new Terraform module variable set (private_controlplane_upgrade.strategy) to express tenant cohorts, priority tiers, and max-concurrent-promotions.
- Extend the control plane operator with "reconciliation batches": a batch is a list of tenant IDs (or tenant selectors), desired version, and an observability gate definition. The operator will advance a batch only if gate conditions are satisfied.
- Canary cohorts selected by: SLA tier (paid > free), observed request volume, and region. Default initial cohort = 5 small paid tenants + 2 internal shadow tenants.
- Telemetry gating: use composite gate evaluated by the rollout controller: (1) error rate delta <= 0.5% absolute, (2) API P95 increase <= 25ms, (3) no new elevated alert severity in the rollout namespace. Gate evaluation window = 10m by default, configurable per rollout.
- Preflight checks run as part of Terraform apply: validate image signatures, verify operator RBAC bindings, ensure KMS key versions and KMS IAM policies in place, confirm control plane CRD schema compatibility.
- Rollback policy: automated rollback if gate fails for two consecutive evaluation windows OR critical alerts fire. Rollback must be recorded with audit entry and optional automated customer notifications for impacted tenants.
- Observability: create rollout dashboard (per-rollout and per-tenant slices), synthetic probes for representative workloads, and export rollout events to audit logs.

Acceptance criteria:
- New Terraform variables and examples added to private_controlplane module and referenced in docs.
- Operator implements batched reconciliation with telemetry gate checks and exposes status conditions on the Rollout CR.
- End-to-end e2e test that simulates a failing canary and verifies automatic rollback.
- Runbook updated with manual abort and emergency rollback steps.
- One successful internal canary rollout executed to production-like environment with telemetry gates enabled.

Implementation notes:
- Prefer adding gate evaluation as a sidecar service in the operator pod to keep reconciliation logic small. Gate engine communicates with TSDB (Prometheus) for metric queries and CloudEvents for alert triggers.
- Use signed artifact verification on images (cosign) before promotion.
- Tenant selectors should support both explicit lists and label selectors (e.g., "tier:enterprise,region:eu").
- Terraform changes must be backward compatible; default strategy = "legacy-wave" to preserve current behavior unless customers opt-in.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: noisy telemetry for small tenants produces false negatives. Mitigation: include minimum traffic thresholds and allow synthetic traffic injection for low-volume tenants.
- Risk: long gate windows delay upgrades. Mitigation: provide override path for emergency toggles with audit trail.
- Risk: Terraform drift between control plane CR state and IaC. Mitigation: reconcile status and surface drift as part of the rollout summary; provide auto-repair option behind a flag.

Open questions:
- Should tenant cohorting be purely customer-configurable or should we provide a recommended policy engine? (PM/Support input required)
- Do we require encrypted per-tenant rollout metadata persisted in the control plane DB?

Docs & artifacts: design doc and rollout runbook linked below.
